captured_note: Ported from the capture's methods/35_vjepa, which wraps the official facebookresearch/jepa repo (it ships no model/loss of its own). The capture has two paths: a pretrain CAVEAT probe of the released V-JEPA VIDEO ViT-H/16 on ImageNet images (explicitly an appendix/caveat row, 'very low accuracy, not a main-table success'), and a step-2 unified-comparison that trains a V-JEPA-objective image ViT-B/16 from scratch on ImageNet at num_frames=1. This port covers the STEP-2 from-scratch path (a genuine comparable row, like 31_dinov3); the pretrain caveat probe is not ported. It pins facebookresearch/jepa as the submodule third_party/jepa and IMPORTS its ViT + predictor (app.vjepa.utils.init_video_model), its 3D mask collator (src.masks.multiblock3d) and apply_masks, running them in a single-process trainer. The port keeps the capture directory numbering (35) per the 2026-08-09 keep-capture-numbering decision (this list's number 33 is V-JEPA -- see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).

paper.title: Revisiting Feature Prediction for Learning Visual Representations from Video (V-JEPA)
paper.authors: Bardes, Garrido, Ponce, Chen, Rabbat, LeCun, Ballas, Assran

upstream.note: The V-JEPA ViT + predictor (app.vjepa.utils.init_video_model, src.models.*), the 3D multi-block mask collator (src.masks.multiblock3d) and apply_masks (src.masks.utils) are imported from this pinned submodule through PYTHONPATH; never copied or installed. The imported src/app modules are torch/torchvision-only (measured). The `src`/`app` imports are lazy (inside run/build) so the in-process test suite stays collision-free with other submodule ports that also expose a `src` package.

scope: The step-2 image adaptation of V-JEPA is ported: a context encoder and an EMA target encoder (the official video ViT + predictor, run at num_frames=1 / tubelet_size=1 so the backbone is an image ViT-B/16) are trained by latent prediction over 3D multi-block masks -- the target encodes the full image, the context encoder sees only the visible (encoder-mask) tokens, and the predictor predicts the target's layer-normalised representations at the masked (predictor-mask) positions (loss = mean over masks of mean|z_pred - target|^loss_exp / loss_exp, plus an optional variance regulariser). AdamW under a warmup+cosine LR schedule; the target encoder is an EMA of the context encoder. The capture's pretrain caveat probe of the released video model is EXCLUDED, as is (implicitly) the video pretraining on VideoMix2M.
encoder: encoder.pt is the EMA target encoder (a bare V-JEPA ViT wrapper, keys backbone.*; there is no separate projection head to exclude). It is the representation V-JEPA evaluation uses; the context encoder and the predictor are training machinery and are not saved. It loads into a rebuilt V-JEPA encoder (build_vjepa_encoder) whose mean-pooled output tokens are the probed feature (embed_dim; 768 for ViT-B).
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the target encoder's mean-pooled tokens (embed_dim), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Images use the deterministic val pipeline (resize + centre crop, ImageNet normalisation). The capture's own V-JEPA eval sweeps several linear-probe LRs with the official probe; this port follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise features, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) instead, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.
rewritten_during_the_port: the capture's pretrain caveat probe of the released VIDEO ViT-H/16 is not ported (the capture itself marks it an appendix/caveat, not a main-table result); the from-scratch step-2 image adaptation on ImageNet is what is ported

the V-JEPA ViT + predictor (init_video_model), the 3D mask collator and apply_masks are imported from the pinned facebookresearch/jepa submodule, never copied; build_vjepa / build_vjepa_encoder wrap init_video_model config-driven so a small hermetic CPU smoke can run a tiny vit_tiny
the src/app imports are lazy (inside run/build functions) so the in-process test suite does not collide with other submodule ports that also expose a top-level `src` package
the model runs at num_frames=1 / tubelet_size=1, so the video ViT is an image ViT; the smoke uses vit_tiny at 64px (a 4x4 patch grid, so the block masks fit)
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA; main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch); the DataLoader gets a seeded generator

the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel and TensorBoard/tqdm, single-process fp32; the latent-prediction loss, the 3D masks, the EMA target and the AdamW warmup+cosine schedule are kept faithfully
encoder.pt is the EMA target encoder; the probe follows the lab's shared ARSSL protocol so the number is comparable across the ported methods
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; the pretrain stage reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
